paragraph: Single-family is the backbone of Lyndhurst with 37 sales over six months at a median of $600,000, mostly three-bedroom colonials and capes with two baths. Roughly 59 percent went above asking and the median sale took 19 days, so this is competitive without being frenzied. Well-priced homes move, and you should expect competition on the good ones. Two-families are the story most outsiders miss here. Twenty-one sold at a median of $850,000, the sale-to-list ratio ran 1.048, and about 71 percent closed above asking, which makes this the tightest tier in town. Condos and townhouses are thin, nine sales at a median of $415,000, typically two-bedroom, two-bath units, and with that few closings you should treat it as a price reference rather than a trend. On the monthly numbers, single-family volume was heaviest in July at nine closings with the median at $640,000, up from the spring, so Lyndhurst is holding firm into the summer peak rather than fading. Monthly counts are small, so read that as direction, not a promise. If you're weighing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and yard of a single-family, the rental income of a two-family, or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo.
